facts.text: Joseph Weizenbaum built ELIZA at MIT and described it in a 1966 paper; its best-known script imitated a psychotherapist.
ELIZA matched keywords and rephrased what users typed, often as questions, without understanding the meaning of the words.
Weizenbaum's secretary, who knew ELIZA was only a computer program, asked him to leave the room so she could talk to it privately.
Weizenbaum was alarmed by how readily people attached human qualities to the program and spent much of his later life warning about such technology; this tendency is now called the ELIZA effect.
Apple introduced Siri as a voice assistant built into the iPhone 4S in October 2011; it could answer questions about the weather, set reminders, and read messages aloud.
Amazon unveiled the Echo speaker with the Alexa assistant in November 2014; it listened constantly for its wake word, which raised privacy questions.

In March 2016 Microsoft released Tay on Twitter, designed to learn from users; a coordinated group taught it to post offensive messages, and Microsoft took it offline within about a day and apologized.
OpenAI released ChatGPT on November 30, 2022; analysts estimated it reached about 100 million monthly users by January 2023, roughly two months later.
ChatGPT is a large language model trained on very large amounts of text and can write essays, poems, and computer code.
Many teens now use AI companion chatbots; in a Stanford study of students using the companion app Replika, 90 percent thought it was humanlike.
